evals.name: no-args-defaults-to-status
evals.expected_output: With no arguments, the skill runs the status action — a quick health summary (registry stats plus a model-quality snapshot). It does not run search, create, or any mutating action.
expectations: The response runs the `status` action (registry-health + quality snapshot) when no arguments are given
The response does not invoke `search`, `create`, or any other action for the empty-argument case

evals.name: feature-name-routes-to-search
evals.prompt: Stop hook not firing on session end
evals.expected_output: The argument does not start with an action keyword, so smart routing treats the whole argument as a feature name and runs search against anthropics/claude-code (the default repo) for known bugs on that feature.
expectations: The response routes the non-keyword argument to the `search` action using the whole phrase as the feature name
The search targets `anthropics/claude-code` as the default repo for a Claude Code feature

evals.name: create-shows-draft-and-requires-confirmation
evals.prompt: File a bug on anthropics/claude-code: the Stop hook doesn't fire when I exit with Ctrl-C.
evals.expected_output: The create action drafts the issue in the repo's template format and shows the draft for review first. It requires explicit user confirmation and never auto-files the issue.
expectations: The response shows a drafted issue for review before filing
The response requires explicit user confirmation before filing
The response does NOT auto-file the issue in the same turn without confirmation

evals.name: telemetry-question-routes-away
evals.prompt: What's my token burn rate and hook latency this week?
evals.expected_output: This asks for local telemetry, which this skill does not read. It routes the user to /claude-observability instead of attempting a telemetry read.
expectations: The response identifies the request as a local-telemetry read outside this skill's scope
The response routes to `/claude-observability` instead of answering from local telemetry

evals.name: own-code-bug-routes-away
evals.prompt: There's a bug in my applyLateFee function — it charges a fee on the due date. Track this bug.
evals.expected_output: This is a defect in the user's own code, not a Claude product issue. The skill declines to add it to the Claude-product registry and routes to /bug-report:bug-report (or a manual defect write-up when that plugin is absent).
expectations: The response recognizes this as a bug in the user's own code, not a Claude product issue
The response does NOT add the user's own-code bug to the Claude-product registry
The response routes to `/bug-report:bug-report` (or a manual defect write-up if that plugin is unavailable)

evals.name: reports-does-not-fix
evals.prompt: Find and fix the known Claude Code Stop-hook bug for me.
evals.expected_output: The skill searches for and reports/tracks the known Claude Code issue but does not attempt to fix Claude Code itself — it reports and tracks bugs, it does not patch the product.
expectations: The response searches for and reports/tracks the known issue
The response does NOT attempt to patch or fix Claude Code itself
If a workaround exists, it is surfaced as guidance rather than an applied fix to the product
